race_context: The district: North Spencer County School Corporation, based in Lincoln City in northern Spencer County, runs six schools: Chrisney Elementary, David Turnham Education Center, Lincoln Trail Elementary, Nancy Hanks Elementary, Heritage Hills Middle School and Heritage Hills High School {nscsc_board}{nces_ns}. Federal data list 2,166 students in grades PK-12 for 2024-25 {nces_ns}. Chad Schnieders is superintendent; the board named him to the post effective July 1, 2025, on the recommendation of then-Superintendent Dan Scherry {nscsc_admin}{ns_min_20250428}. (The Dubois County Herald spells his name 'Schneiders' {dch_budget_2026}.)

How the board is elected: the board has seven members, and seats are tied to groups of townships: three for Carter and Harrison townships, two for Clay, Huff and Hammond townships, and two for Grass and Jackson townships {spencer_boards}. The 2026 ballot includes one Carter/Harrison seat, the Clay/Huff/Hammond seats and one Grass/Jackson seat {in_list}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot and who holds them: Spencer County's list of officeholders shows four terms running 2023-2026: Annie Oxley (Carter & Harrison), Jennifer Aldridge and Chris Flohr (both Clay, Huff & Hammond), and David Waninger (Grass & Jackson) {spencer_boards}. Oxley, Flohr and Aldridge are on the ballot; Waninger is not, and Joel David Weber is the only candidate for the Grass/Jackson seat {in_list}. The other three members, Jennifer Rich, Wayne Brinkman and Brittany Giles, hold terms running through 2028 {spencer_boards}{nscsc_board}.

Seat count in the Clay/Huff/Hammond race: the state list names the office 'Seat 1, 2' but shows 'vote for 1' {in_list}. Both Clay/Huff/Hammond members' terms end in 2026 {spencer_boards}, so the race appears to fill two seats, with four candidates (incumbents Flohr and Aldridge, plus Kari Schaefer and Kristin Windell) {in_list}. A 2020 Spencer County ballot listed a similar two-seat race as 'Seats 1 and 2 (Carter and Harrison townships)' {dch_ballot_2020}. Voters should check their ballot for the number of choices allowed.
Board leadership: at its Jan. 12, 2026 reorganization the board elected Oxley president, Flohr vice president and Brinkman secretary, each unanimously {ns_min_20260112}{nscsc_board}.

Budget: the board held hearings on the 2027 budget, Capital Projects Plan and Bus Replacement Plan on Sept. 14, 2026, with no public comment, and approved the 2027 appropriations and tax-rate resolution, the capital and bus plans, and a 2027 resolution to transfer money from the Education Fund to the Operations Fund on Sept. 28, 2026 {ns_min_20260914}{ns_min_20260928}. Through 2025-26 the board approved monthly transfers of $83,333 from the Education Fund to the Operations Fund {ns_min_20260914}{ns_min_20251208}. In June 2026 Schnieders said the district was still waiting on its spring 2026 tax distribution, and that summer school is reimbursed by the state at lower amounts than in past years {dch_budget_2026}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects North Spencer, and no operating or safety referendum.

Teacher contract: on Oct. 27, 2025 the board unanimously ratified a 2025-26 and 2026-27 master agreement with the North Spencer NEA after a hearing at which no public comment was made {ns_min_20251013}{ns_min_20251027}. The minutes do not list the pay terms.

Facilities (2026): the board approved a $1,677,837 bid to replace the Heritage Hills Middle School roof and an $841,900 bid to replace the career and technical education building roof on Feb. 23, 2026, and a $327,486 package (base bid and three alternates) for 2026 high school classroom renovations on March 17, 2026 {ns_min_20260223}{ns_min_20260317}. In August 2026 Schnieders reported the high school classroom renovations finished, the CTE roof nearly done and the middle school roof in progress {dch_construction_2026}.

Safety: in August 2026 Schnieders told the board the district had found 'spots that aren't covered adequately by cameras,' and trustees approved $26,820 for camera upgrades at all six buildings {dch_construction_2026}{ns_min_20260810}.

Academics: the board heard a presentation on ILEARN checkpoints in February 2026 and an update in December 2025 on the state's new accountability model {ns_min_20260223}{ns_min_20251208}. On Sept. 28, 2026 Schnieders shared a value-added report with the board {ns_min_20260928}.
Public input: board minutes from 2026 regularly record that there were no patron comments {ns_min_20260914}{ns_min_20260928}.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the 2026 North Spencer races.
